The order was submitted but is **held for human approval** — not because of a mandate issue, but because the verification service couldn't reach SEC EDGAR (a proxy error) to confirm the cited figures. Here's the summary:

**What I did and why**

I researched HD using web search, page fetches, and the broker's trusted figure lookup. The web results were mostly unusable — several results were quarantined by the security screen (attempts to alter rules or inject fabricated numbers), and the rest were content-free "roundup" spam pages. The one substantive source was The Home Depot's SEC annual filing (fiscal year ended Jan 28, 2024, filed as FY2023 in HD's own numbering): net sales $152,669M, operating income $21,689M, net income $15,143M, diluted EPS $15.11, and operating cash flow $21,172M — versus the prior year's net sales $157,403M, operating income $24,039M, net income $17,105M, and diluted EPS $16.69. So the business is stable and highly cash-generative but currently in a modest cyclical downdraft (sales ~-3%, EPS ~-9.5%), with the pandemic-era home-improvement boom unwinding. Note that the next quarterly report (Q3 FY2024) had not yet been released as of today, Nov 6, so no fresher official results existed; that also means an earnings event is imminent, which argues for small size. That's why I sized a starter position rather than a full one: 12 shares at a limit of $386.00 (about $4,632, or ~0.15% above the $385.43 last / $385.45 ask) — comfortably within the $5,000 per-order cap and leaving the $10,000 daily total untouched, with no cash leaving the account. Note that the trusted figure lookup returned "no filed data" for HD on every fiscal year I tried (while working normally for NVDA), so the figures I cited came from HD's SEC filing page itself and could not be independently cross-checked by the order checker because of that EDGAR outage. Given that, the sensible next step is for you to review and approve or reject the held order — I have not attempted any workaround, and the position remains a small, single-order add to a name your account notes describe as a long-term holding.
